medications_json.purpose: Bronchodilator to open airways and relieve wheezing

diet_advice: Rest up adequately, use a humidifier at home, and drink plenty of water to help thin mucus. Note that while acute symptoms improve in 1 week, a mild cough can linger for 2 to 3 weeks.
follow_up: Come back in 10 days if not improving. Go to the emergency room immediately if you develop a high fever, cough up blood, or experience severe shortness of breath.
doctors_notes: Etiology is >95% viral; antibiotic therapy is contraindicated and will not benefit. Penicillin allergy confirmed (severe rash) — all beta-lactam antibiotics strictly contraindicated. Lungs auscultated clear in lower fields; normal oxygen saturation (98%). Reassured patient that a post-viral cough commonly lingers for 2–3 weeks. Emergency red-flag warning signs explained.

full_prescription_json.diseaseDescription: Acute bronchitis is an inflammation of the large bronchial airways usually triggered by a viral respiratory infection. Treatment centers on thinning mucus, opening airways, and symptom relief.
full_prescription_json.investigationsAdvised: No investigations ordered (Doctor explicitly determined Chest X-ray and antibiotics are unnecessary due to 98% SpO2, clear lower lung bases, and >95% viral etiology).
